properties.name: Harappa
properties.notes: Eponymous type site of the Harappan civilization; on the Ravi. Excavated 1920-21 to 1933-34 (Vats) and 1986-2001 (HARP).
sources: Vats, M.S. 1940. Excavations at Harappa, Vol. I (text), Vol. II (139 plates). Govt. of India Press. — title page (site name); Plate I (site plan; georeferenced for coordinates and mound polygons)

IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5 (Dr. Avantika Sharma): 'Harappa was excavated in 1920 by Daya Ram Sahni'; 'following the archaeological convention of naming a culture where it was first discovered'; chronology table lists Harappa under Early (3300-2600 BCE), Mature (2600-1800 BCE), Late ('Cemetery H at Harappa')

Harappa Archaeological Research Project (HARP), harappa.com/indus4/e1.html: Period 1 Ravi/Hakra (>3500-2800 BC), Period 2 Kot Diji (2800-2600 BC), Period 3 Harappa phase (2600-1900 BC), Period 5 Late Harappa (c.1800-<1300 BC)
Kenoyer 2008 (Sackler Colloquium, harappa.com PDF): city grew to 150 ha in the Harappa phase; Dales & Kenoyer 1990: areal extent ~150 ha; Vats 1940:3: site ~3.5 miles 'in circuit'
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to excavation report, excavation project, or national university course material.
properties.coordinate_provenance: Derived: Vats 1940 Plate I georeferenced (1000-ft grid scale + north-arrow rotation 2.96 deg + OSM Harappa Museum anchor); site centroid = mean of mound-area centroids. Method documented in mound_areas.geojson properties.

properties.name: Mohenjo-daro
properties.notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site no. 138 (inscribed 1980; State Party Pakistan). Western citadel sector with eastern lower city on the Indus; streets at right angles with sanitation and drainage. Located in Larkana district, Sindh. Spelling follows the excavation report; UNESCO renders "Moenjodaro".
sources: Marshall, John (ed.) 1931. Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization, Vol. III (plates). Arthur Probsthain, London — title page: 'official account of Archaeological Excavations at Mohenjo-daro carried out by the Government of India between the years 1922 and 1927' (artifact in hand: data/artifacts/marshall1931_djvu.txt)

UNESCO World Heritage Centre periodic-reporting document, Geographic Information Table for property 138 (whc.unesco.org/document/164707): coordinates 27.329N 68.139E; property 240 ha; UNESCO International Safeguarding Campaign 1974-1997
IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5: 'Mohenjodaro [excavated] by Rakhaldas Banerjee in 1921'; chronology table lists Mohenjodaro under Mature Harappan (2600-1800 BCE) only; Larkana district, Sindh
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to the excavation report, UNESCO listing, or national university course material. Early/late occupation unverified (Marshall's scheme predates the modern framework); "largest city" claim dropped as uncited; 240 ha is the WH property boundary, not the archaeological footprint.
properties.coordinate_provenance: Official UNESCO property coordinates (periodic-reporting Geographic Information Table, property 138); property-centroid, not a field-survey pin.

properties.name: Rakhigarhi
properties.notes: One of the largest cities of the Harappan Civilization (Hisar district, Haryana); seven mounds over ~300 ha. ASI 1997-2000 fieldwork found planned mud/burnt-brick townships, drainage, fortification, and a bead-manufacturing industry. No decline-phase evidence.
sources: Nath, Amarendra. Excavations at Rakhigarhi [1997-98 to 1999-2000], ASI (draft report submitted 31.12.2014) — Ch. 6: site at 29°17′30″N 76°06′50″E; habitation deposit of two cultural periods, early Harappan (Period I: preformative IA, formative IB) and mature Harappan (Period II); 'no evidence of the decline phase'; archaeological residue 'spreads over in area of 3 Km radius (300 hectare)' over seven mounds

Shinde, V.S. et al. 2018. 'Archaeological and anthropological studies on the Harappan cemetery of Rakhigarhi, India,' PLoS ONE 13(2): e0192299 — RGR-07 necropolis N29°17′52.9″ E76°06′51″; 'one of the largest cities of the Harappan Civilization'
Govt. of India, Ministry of Culture, Lok Sabha Unstarred Q. 4977 (26.03.2018): excavation at Rakhigarhi, District Hissar, Haryana, 1997-98 to 1999-2000
IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5: 'Rakhigarhi (as large as Harappa)'; Banawali and Rakhigarhi in Haryana
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to ASI report, peer-reviewed paper, or parliamentary record. The widely repeated ~350 ha figure is unverified (media attribution, not ASI/peer-reviewed); PIB 22.06.2026 says ~550 ha — conflicting figures; ASI report's own 300 ha cited as primary.
properties.coordinate_provenance: ASI Rakhigarhi report Ch. 6, "Archaeological residue at Rakhigarhi": 29°17′30″N 76°06′50″E from the 1997-2000 survey; corroborated by Shinde et al. 2018 (RGR-07 necropolis). The 1915 Survey of India toposheet figure (29°16′N 76°10′E) is ~7 km off and not used.

properties.name: Kalibangan
properties.notes: Fortified pre-Harappan settlement (Kalibangan I) below the Harappan citadel and lower town (Kalibangan II), in Rajasthan on the Ghaggar. Outstanding discoveries: a ploughed field southeast of the Period I settlement, and rows of fire altars (KLB-1 citadel, KLB-3). Excavated 1960-61 to 1969-70 (ASI, B.B. Lal & B.K. Thapar).
sources: Thapar, B.K. 1975. 'Kalibangan: A Harappan Metropolis Beyond the Indus Valley,' Expedition 17(2): 19-32 (co-excavator's account) — Kalibangan I (pre-Harappan) and Kalibangan II (Harappan); Period II radiocarbon bracket 2300-1750 BCE; mound dimensions (Period I ~250x160 m; citadel ~240x120 m; lower city ~240x360 m); ploughed field; fire altars
Lal, B.B. et al. 2003. Excavations at Kalibangan: The Early Harappans (1960-1969), MASI No. 98, ASI — final report (Early Harappan Period I); Mature Harappan Period II in the follow-up volume
IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5: Kalibangan in Rajasthan; listed under Mature Harappan; 'Excavations began at Kalibangan in 1960s and continued for a decade'
properties.authority_note: Periods, size, excavation status, and description verified (Thapar 1975; ASI 2003; IGNOU Unit 5). COORDINATES UNVERIFIED — shown as provisional dot only. The absolute date "c. 2800 BCE" for the ploughed field is unverified.
properties.coordinate_provenance: PROVISIONAL — unverified. No digitized copy of the 2003 ASI report found; no coordinate figure in accessible ASI Indian Archaeology—A Review volumes or peer-reviewed papers. Placeholder pending the 2003 report's location plan or a GPS-verified survey figure.

properties.name: Dholavira
properties.notes: Tripartite fortified Harappan city (citadel, middle town, lower town) with elaborate reservoir-based water harvesting; ten large Indus-script gypsum inlays ("signboard") at the North Gate. Excavated 1989-90 to 2004-05 (ASI, R.S. Bisht).
sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: 'Dholavira: A Harappan City', inscribed 2021, 44COM 8B.35, ref. 1645 — official property name
UNESCO nomination table, doc 187795 (properties examined 2021): centre point N23 53 18.27 E70 12 47.89 (= 23.8884, 70.2133); inscribed area 103 ha

Bisht, R.S. 2015. Excavations at Dholavira (1989-2005). ASI — reservoirs (§pp.148,164 per public copy); signboard (§8.1.1, pp.228-231 per public copy); seven cultural stages, occupation through 3rd millennium into mid-2nd millennium BCE

Bisht lecture, IIT Gandhinagar, 18 Oct 2013 ('Dholavira: A Unique Harappan City'): 13 field seasons 1989-90 to 2004-05; 'one amongst five largest urban centers of Harappan civilization' (with Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ganweriwala, Rakhigarhi)
IGNOU eGyankosh BHIC-101E Unit 5: Dholavira among Gujarat Harappan sites; listed under Mature Harappan and in Transitional Phase row
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to UNESCO listing/dossier, ASI excavation report, or excavator's lecture. Discovery (1968, J.P. Joshi) unverified — omitted.
properties.coordinate_provenance: Centre point of the inscribed UNESCO property as filed in India's January 2020 nomination dossier (table doc 187795); not a surveyed city centre but property-scale, adequate for a site dot.

properties.name: Lothal
properties.notes: Port town with dockyard; bead-making center.
sources: Rao, ASI
properties.authority_note: Coordinates and description are provisional, drawn from general knowledge; not yet traced to an authoritative source. Do not cite.

properties.harappan_connection: A square Indus stamp seal with an elephant and an eight-sign Indus inscription was excavated at Gonur by V.I. Sarianidi in 2004 (Sarianidi 2005, fig. 114); its sign sequences are paralleled in the Indus valley (Parpola 2006, via Kaniuth & Shaydullaev 2022). Elephant-ivory working at Gonur independently attests Indus contact (Frenez 2018).
properties.name: Gonur Tepe
properties.notes: BMAC (Oxus civilization) center in the Murghab delta, Margiana, Turkmenistan; probable capital of ancient Margush. 60 radiocarbon dates place occupation at 2300-1500 cal BCE.
sources: Kufterin, V. & Dubova, N.A. 2013. 'A preliminary analysis of Late Bronze Age human skeletal remains from Gonur-depe, Turkmenistan' (peer-reviewed): site at 38°12′50″N 62°02′15″E; 2300-1500 cal BCE (60 C14 dates); central part ~25 ha, necropolis ~12 ha; 'probably the capital city of the ancient state of Margush'; excavated by the Margiana expedition under V.I. Sarianidi
Pleiades Gazetteer: 'Gonur Tepe: a Pleiades place resource' (McKee et al. 2025), pleiades.stoa.org/places/391537222 — canonical name form

Kaniuth, M. & Shaydullaev, Sh. 2022. 'The Sapalli culture seal corpus,' CISI 3.3 (peer-reviewed corpus): Indus seal excavated by Sarianidi 2004, elephant + eight-sign inscription paralleled in the Indus valley (Parpola 2006)

Parpola, A. 2018. 'Indus Seals and Glyptic Studies: An Overview' (Univ. of Helsinki): 'In 2004, a square Indus seal with elephant and a line of Indus script with native Harappan sequences was excavated at Gonur'
Frenez, D. 2018. 'Manufacturing and trade of Asian elephant ivory in Bronze Age Middle Asia: Evidence from Gonur Depe,' Archaeological Research in Asia 15 (peer-reviewed)
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to peer-reviewed publications or the Pleiades gazetteer. Full title of "Sarianidi 2005" not verified in this pass; Temple of Water findspot via secondary citation.
properties.coordinate_provenance: Expedition-published site center (Kufterin & Dubova 2013, Introduction); corroborated by Pleiades representative point.

properties.harappan_connection: Sixteen Indus-style seals excavated at Ur: published by C.J. Gadd 1932 ("Seals of ancient Indian style found at Ur," Proc. British Academy XVIII); four from the Royal Cemetery (UE 2, Woolley 1934); nine catalogued UE 10 (Legrain 1951, Cat. 624-632). UE 10 Introductory Note: they "prove the existence of early trade relations between the Indus valley and lower Mesopotamia."
properties.name: Ur
properties.notes: Sumerian city-state at modern Tell el-Muqayyar, Dhi Qar, Iraq; Ur III ziggurat of Nanna still stands. First excavated 1850s (Taylor); 1922-1934 joint UPenn/British Museum expedition (Woolley). Inscribed within UNESCO WH ref 1481 (Ahwar of Southern Iraq, 2016) as "Ur Archaeological City".
periods: Ubaid to Neo-Babylonian (5th mill. BCE - 539 BCE); floruit Early Dynastic III / Ur III (2100-2000 BCE)
sources: CDLI Wiki (Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative, Oxford/UCLA/MPIWG): 'Ur (modern Tell Muqayyar)' — coords 30°57′45.55″N 46°6′11.03″E; occupied Ubaid to Neo-Babylonian; city ~50 ha in Ur III; excavation history (Taylor 1850s; Woolley 1922-1934)
Gadd, C.J. 1932. 'Seals of ancient Indian style found at Ur,' Proceedings of the British Academy, vol. XVIII (22 pp., 3 pls.) — 16 Indus-style seals at Ur
Legrain, L. 1951. Seal Cylinders, Ur Excavations vol. 10 (British Museum / Univ. Museum Philadelphia; OUP) — Cat. 624-632; Introductory Note on Indus-Mesopotamia trade
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to CDLI or the Ur Excavations volumes. Gadd 1932 paper cited via UE 10's own footnote (not read in full); individual seal U.7683/BM 120573 claims left out (non-authoritative sources only).
properties.coordinate_provenance: CDLI (Oxford/UCLA/MPIWG consortium) gazetteer coordinates for Tell Muqayyar.

properties.harappan_connection: First Indus-inspired circular 'Gulf-type' stamp seals appear in layers contemporary with the city-wall construction c. 2050 BCE, some with short Indus-script inscriptions; simultaneous adoption of a formal weight system — cubical/spherical stone weights matching Harappan standard units (the 'Tilmun norm', na Tilmun, UET 5 796); square polished weights of Indus origin also reported (Laursen & Steinkeller 2017; Crawford 2001).
properties.name: Qal'at al-Bahrain
properties.notes: Tell on Bahrain's north coast, capital of the Dilmun polity and entrepôt in Mesopotamia-Indus Gulf trade (UNESCO: 'traded with the Indus Valley and Mesopotamia'). Danish excavations since 1954 (Bibby); published Højlund & Andersen 1994. UNESCO WH ref 1192ter, inscribed 2005. 'Dilmun' is the Bronze-Age polity; Qal'at al-Bahrain is the excavated site.
periods: occupied 2300 BCE - 16th c. CE; Indus-contact horizon c. 2050 BCE (Early Dilmun)
sources: UNESCO World Heritage List ref 1192ter: 'Qal`at al-Bahrain – Ancient Harbour and Capital of Dilmun', inscribed 2005 — official name; 'occupied since at least 2300 BCE'; 'traded with the Indus Valley and Mesopotamia'
UNESCO nomination dossier, doc. 168878, §2.4: core zone spans 26°14′04″N–26°13′53″N, 50°31′06″E–50°31′28″E (center ≈ 26°14′01″N 50°31′14″E); §2.6: core zone 16.3 ha

Laursen, S. & Steinkeller, P. 2017. Babylonia, the Gulf Region, and the Indus (Mesopotamian Civilizations 20, Eisenbrauns) — Gulf-type seals c. 2050 BCE; Harappan-standard weights; Tilmun norm (UET 5 796)
Højlund, F. & Andersen, H.H. 1994. Qala'at al-Bahrain vol. 1 (Jutland Archaeological Society / Moesgaard Museum) — excavation report; square polished Indus weights p. 118
Crawford, H. 2001. 'Early Dilmun Seals From Saar,' Archaeology International (UCL, peer-reviewed)
properties.authority_note: All fields traced to UNESCO listing/dossier or peer-reviewed monographs. Full Danish/French/local campaign chronology not verified in this pass; Laursen & Steinkeller p. 50 via published excerpt.
properties.coordinate_provenance: UNESCO nomination dossier (doc. 168878) core-zone coordinates; representative center of the 16.3 ha core zone. Supersedes the old gazetteer value, which was ~25 km off (in the sea).

properties.notes: Northernmost Harappan outpost (Afghanistan); lapis lazuli trade.
sources: Francfort

metadata.verification_policy: Authoritative sources only: excavation reports, national archaeological surveys, UNESCO listings, national heritage registries, peer-reviewed gazetteers. Wikipedia, journalism, and model training data do not qualify. Entries are 'unverified' until every field traces to such a source.
